## Outcome follow-up scheduler

n8n is the clock; the work happens in JS.

Every five minutes in Australia/Melbourne this calls
`POST /api/followup-tick` on the portal, which:

- sends outcome checks whose `followup_due_at` has passed
- closes commitment/outcome windows that expired unanswered
  as `NO_FEEDBACK` (never `NOT_YET`)
- writes **only** `schedule_state` — the delayed check is a
  feedback event, never a clinician-approved nudge

### Requires exactly ONE n8n variable

**`FOLLOWUP_TICK_SECRET`** — must match the value set on Vercel
Production, or every tick returns 401. It is in `local/n8n.env`.

`PORTAL_BASE_URL` is OPTIONAL. It defaults to the production
portal and only needs setting to point somewhere else.

No Google or Twilio credentials are needed here — this workflow
has no Sheets nodes at all. Those live on Vercel now.

### Reading a run
The HTTP response is the summary: `sent`, `expired_commitment`,
`expired_outcome`, `failed`. A green run with `sent: 0` means
nothing was due, which is the normal case.

### Why only three nodes
The previous 16-node version is archived at
`docs/archive/workflow_f_followup_n8n_native.json` — do NOT
import it. Its logic was 120 lines of Code plus 19 IF conditions
and column mappings, and only the first was testable. The same
logic now lives in `landing/api/_lib/followup-scheduler.js` with
ordinary unit tests. Vercel Hobby caps cron at once per day, so
the clock stays here where five-minute scheduling is free.

Ships inactive.
